title: The State of Markets

reader_summary.headline: The fastest AI companies are hitting $100 million in revenue faster than any SAS company ever did.
reader_summary.overview: The fastest AI companies are hitting $100 million in revenue faster than any SAS company ever did. The top performers grew 693% year over year in 2025, generating up to a million dollars in revenue per employee. That's not some efficiency playbook.

key_points.text: The fastest AI companies are hitting $100 million in revenue faster than any SAS company ever did.
key_points.evidence_quote: The fastest AI companies are hitting $100 million in revenue faster than any SAS company ever did, and they're spending less on sales and marketing to get there.

key_points.text: Demand is so strong these companies can barely keep up.
key_points.evidence_quote: Demand is so strong these companies can barely keep up.

key_points.text: On the supply side, every GPU that gets plugged in is maxed out immediately, but there are cracks.
key_points.evidence_quote: On the supply side, every GPU that gets plugged in is maxed out immediately, but there are cracks.

key_points.text: Dead is entering the system, and the biggest thing holding back enterprise adoption isn't the tech itself.

thesis: The speakers argue that the fastest-growing AI companies are achieving significantly higher revenue growth and efficiency than previous SaaS companies because of extremely strong customer demand and lower spending on sales and marketing. They conclude that the current market is at the very beginning of a 10 to 15-year product cycle, requiring existing businesses to natively incorporate AI or face obsolescence.
